```{r,echo=FALSE}
rm = sample(2:9,2)*sample(c(-1,1),2,T)
cn = function(real,imag){
    ss = paste0("{",real,"}+",imag,"i")
    ss = gsub("+-","-",ss,fixed=T)
    ss = gsub("+1i","+i",ss,fixed=T)
    ss = gsub("-1i","-i",ss,fixed=T)
    ss = gsub("+0i","",ss,fixed=T)
    ss = gsub("{0}+","",ss,fixed=T)
    ss = gsub("{0}-","",ss,fixed=T)
    ss = gsub("{","",ss,fixed=T)
    ss = gsub("}","",ss,fixed=T)
    return(ss)
}

R = rm[1]
M = rm[2]

cn1 = cn(R,M)
cn2 = cn(R,-M)

```

Question
========

Let function $f$ be a polynomial with real coefficients. If $f(`r cn1`)=0$, then that implies that $`r cn1`$ is one root of the polynomial.

What is the other known root?

Solution
========

When a polynomial with real coefficients has a complex root, we know the [complex conjugate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_conjugate) is also a root.

So, the answer is ``r cn2``
